name: grain
description: Ask a repository about its own conventions before writing code: where <intent> (where such things live, what is expected there, exemplars to copy), what <term> (every place a name or value carries meaning, with siblings and history), how <query> (what a change like this one has looked like before), check <file> (how a file sits against the local norm), review (the same, for your whole change at once), completeness <file> (what historically co-changes with it), spectrum <file>, status/report/rules, export (the whole model as JSON for training pipelines), decide steer|boundary|waive (a committed maintainer decision that steers a pattern) — plus hooks that speak unbidden and an MCP server exposing the same read-only answers to any tool. Statistical answers mined from the repo's syntax trees and full git history; no model calls, no network, never blocks.
